title: Advice to young players: learn the instrument, learn to read
summary: He advises learning to handle the instrument and to read, discusses reading versus improvising on the Morton dates, and dislikes bop's complexity.

bands.name: Jelly Roll Morton's Red Hot Peppers

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: I wondered if you, uh, what advice you would have for somebody, some kid that's going to go into jazz playing. Today, if you should learn to read right away or start to think or what do you think?

No, I, I, I don't know. I, I think, uh, I think you should learn to read and learn, first of all, learn the instrument. You know, learn how to handle the instrument. Yeah, handle the instrument. Yeah, that, I think that's the main thing. Learn how to handle that instrument and then, then, stuff

because if you've got ideas, I think, you'll be able to put them over much better if you can handle, able to handle the instrument. But then too, some say that if you learn to read, it takes something from, you know, that ideas that you've got. I've heard people say it too, but I don't know. I don't know about that, because I hear a lot of guys that's got some good ideas, and the ideas, they can't make them sound like anything because they can't handle the instrument.
You did pretty well, and you learned to read first, and it didn't seem to hold you back.
I think that's better, is to learn to read.

On those Jelly Roll Martin records, I still can't tell sometimes if you've started reading the parts, or it sounds to me like you're improvising the whole thing. Yeah, well, he'd write out the parts that...

I imagine some whole choruses, you didn't even look at the music, did you? Well, no, after I tried to learn the choruses, you know, and try to put in what little ideas that would come to me. Yeah, so I don't know, but I could never, never play like, get the ideas that I, you know, that some of those fellas, you know, play those things like some of those fellas. Well, I think that... Some of those fellas could play a little life out of it.
Yeah, but some of those simple parts that you played were better. They, you stick to the melody, and people know what you're playing.
Like this bop stuff they do today is so complicated, you can't tell what they're playing. That's right, that's right.
